english_verification.review_scope: Checked the current Mod's A82 identity, 1444 history, Napesbay localisation, the two A82-specific Luna missions, A82 national ideas, the shared Luna mission context, and successor B59 idea terminology. Read the related Luna River and Pírluna River Wiki chunks. This is not an exhaustive audit of every mission, event, formation condition, or B59 route.
english_verification.shared_text_integration: The primary read the native B59 appendix, Curtain Call tooltip and Pashainé formation block while assembling the shared article; these are bounded integration checks, not a full successor mission audit.
unresolved: The dedicated Free City of Napesbay Wiki pages are present in the local corpus (page 791) but were not read in this bounded check; wiki_status remains related_only.
The Luna River and Pírluna River pages provide geographic and city context, not proof of A82-specific current mechanics.
The source article's shared narrative, maps, score table, and B59 formation details are handled in the shared article by the primary agent; this overlay preserves only A82 text fields.
The inherited source descriptions and effect displays are translated faithfully; current Mod scripts were checked for terminology, but no source-data or unit correction was made.

rationale.campaign_length: 20 shared missions and 2 specific missions; forming B59 switches to another mission tree.
rationale.colonization: This prelude has no colonial main line.
rationale.complexity: Naval economy and the Luna Sway system must be managed together.
rationale.dark_story: The focus is post-war autonomy and practical trade, not a dark narrative.
rationale.difficulty: Maritime trade and politics require investment; community difficulty assessments are only contextual.
rationale.diplomacy: The Emperor, neighbouring cities, Sway, and the alliance remain the common axis.
rationale.early_pressure: With only one province, it must use port income and Imperial relations to survive.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: No country-specific gameplay is built around spellcasting or artificery.
rationale.narrative_density: The old fleet, the Lilac Wars, and the valley alliance form a continuous story.
rationale.tall_play: One-province port, production, and arsenal development stand out.
rationale.trade_economy: The fleet, merchant privileges, delta economy, and trade rights are the defining themes.
rationale.warfare: The specific fleet and coastal defence matter, while land warfare still serves the shared city integration route.

identity.appearance: A Republican Free City in 1444 and one of the four Luna countries in the scoring table.
identity.region: Pírluna River / East Dameshead / Empire of Anbennar

successors.relationship: The final shared Luna mission unlocks the formation conditions; the decision changes the Tag and switches to a country-specific mission tree.

survey_region.note: Shared source row: Luna River Minors (Rank 3; Region EoA). The original table aggregates the four local Luna countries; this mapping does not claim that they are one EU4 country.

national_ideas.scope_note: Country traditions, seven national ideas, and ambition only; optional idea groups and species/government bonuses are excluded. Multiple candidates and conditions are listed separately and are not treated as simultaneous; whether the new ideas are accepted on formation depends on the actual event/decision and player choice.

description.text: To prevent complete Damerian domination of the seas the old kingdom of Verne had established a bustling arsenal in Napesbay. Though the kingdom might've fallen long ago the infrastructure still stands, allowing us to continue producing vessels at a rapid rate, albeit under a different liege.
description.text_en: To prevent complete Damerian domination of the seas the old kingdom of Verne had established a bustling arsenal in Napesbay. Though the kingdom might've fallen long ago the infrastructure still stands, allowing us to continue producing vessels at a rapid rate, albeit under a different liege.

description.text: Pirates of the Damesneck know to steer clear of Napesbayer vessels, for many a villainous corsair has been sent the sea floor by our guns over the centuries.
description.text_en: Pirates of the Damesneck know to steer clear of Napesbayer vessels, for many a villainous corsair has been sent the sea floor by our guns over the centuries.

description.text:
For centuries Napesbay was the home of the secondary Imperial fleet, frequently referred to as the Napesfleet, mirroring Neckcliffe across the Damesneck. When the Lilac Wars came roaring however, we knew that the fleet would only serve to make us a target should it remain in the hands of the Emperor. Thus, when the order came for the ships to leave port our officials seized the ships, declaring them property of the city and chasing down the ones that attempted to flee. While the Silmuna were understandably upset, bigger problems drew their attention from us and the fleet of Neckcliffe served well in our stead.

For most of the conflict anyway.

description.text: Along the gentle and slow-moving Pírluna are vineyards and wineries, tranquil slices of land owned by retired adventurers from Menibór. With a countryside more akin to the estate of a Wine Lord, they're one of the main employers in Napesbay, only after the arsenal and the navy.

description.text: Ruben of Napesbay was a daring and dashing captain, who led the colonial efforts of Verne, becoming one of the most famous explorers in Cannor. He of course didn't forget his home city, returning with gold and silver to establish a new colonial trading company in Napesbay, bringing trade from Aelantir back home.

description.text: Many of the pirate captains the captains of Napesbay captures are quite skilled, and it would be a waste to not make use of their talents. By establishing a rehabilitation program we can turn these rowdy raiders into proud admirals of the Napesfleet, fighting to finally rid the sea of their former comrades.

description.text: With the Napesbay Company running well and the Napesfleet keeping the seas clear of piracy, Napesbay has swiftly grown into one of the most prominent ports in the Damesneck. Many of the adventurers and settlers flocking to Aelantir leave Cannor through our city, and countless more have been moving here to establish new businesses, at home and abroad. Truly, this is Napesbay's golden age.

description.text:
“The imitation of style necessitates the imitation of form, and therefore of function. When we build a colonnade inspired by the formal markets of Old Dameria, we are inspired also by the conversation held along that colonnade, the type of life enabled by the structure we seek to recreate. The rhetorical tradition, the vibrant public life, even the raucous protest – all are made possible by the decision, made once again, to build space for them.”
Saman of Fowlbarn, ‘The Life Of Stone’

description.text:
“Even in those realms which had not subordinated their government to an association of guild-backed aldermen, the Guild had been the fundamental unit of urban life in the Eastern Dameshead long before Pashainé’s emergence as a coherent state.

This had three major consequences. First, the codification of a sort of corporate democracy, a belief that society was best forged under a competing set of mutually-exerted pressures, by groups representing collectives of the population - even if these were subject to a monarch or a so-called ’Executive Guild’. Second, an emphasis on economic prosperity, the brass tacks ‘shopkeeper diplomacy’ for which Pashainé became notorious. Third, a relentless focus on urbanisation and the vertical integration of industry.”
Silvard Dove, ‘An Economic History of Cannor’

description.text:
“The poet Milian said that the Pashainéy is uniquely noble, having inherited the bravery of his Vernman father and the dignity of his Damerian mother. As a second daughter, I seem to have been left with the libido and stubbornness.”
Genaia ‘Geni’ Cadesna sina Bellacaire, ‘Memoirs Of A Fallen Countess’

description.text:
“Consider the conflict between Corinism and the Court which had so split the Valley. Consider, then, an unusually literate and engaged populace with a political impetus to see theological ruptures healed. Consider finally the Ravelian Lodge, which in its structure mimics the voluntary association basis of the guild. No population on Halann was more ready to embrace not merely the articles of belief but the basic organisational structure of Ravelianism.”
Leande Bellac, ‘Apologetics’

description.text:
“Over the course of the eighteenth century, the slowly aggregating impact of the Verdancy became more and more clear across the entire Luna watershed. Land which had once been among the most fertile in Cannor gave harvest perhaps once in two years, while the concomitant soil pollution devastated the Valley’s few remaining natural forests. The result was an exodus of the population from the countryside and an even greater urbanisation of Pashainé, inadvertently birthing a contentious café and street culture; this would dominate the labour politics of the following hundred years, erupting again and again into civil unrest. You will find few along the Valley who have much to say in praise of Camir Silmuna, but our land is indelibly marked by his legacy.”
Lucas síl Bellacaire, The History of the Lilac River, Vol. II

description.text:
“Do not fear death, my people. Fear nothing which you do in the company of brave souls; fear nothing which you do among your fellow citizens! We live in the time of the Mage-Emperors – in the era of the staff – and its power seems absolute. But we know these mages can die.

We knew it three hundred years ago, when the discipline of the fusillade first began to rival the arc of the fireball. We knew it two hundred years ago, when first we learned of that glorious substance, then accessible only so very far away, which could countermand their unearned gifts. And we know it now – now that their ritual of growth, their promise of endless harvest, has wrought a desolate steppe where once there was only verdant life. It is what they do! Addle the land, poison the water, wreck the bountiful Halann we share for the slightest chance at a lonely throne.

Hear me! It’s true – we may die today. But we die together, while they die alone.”
Carric of Paredocks, Final Address

player_overview.avoid_if: You want to start with a large fleet or pursue only rapid overland expansion.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Start from a one-province port, fleet, and trade; use Sway and diplomacy to integrate the Luna, then decide whether to form Pashainé.
player_overview.overview: You begin as Napesbay of Vernman culture: vineyards, delta trade, and the old arsenal give it the strongest maritime identity among the four Luna Free Cities. Repair the city, build light ships, and restore the fleet, then use Luna Sway to manage the Emperor and neighbouring cities; eventually federate the cities into Pashainé.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy ports, fleets, merchant politics, and high-development small-state diplomacy.
signature_features: Two specific missions revolve around light ships, an admiral, and the old arsenal.
The port and Pírluna Valley give maritime trade and coastal defence a distinctive position.
It shares 20 Luna alliance missions with the other Free Cities and can form B59.
player_overview.tagline: Build ships and trade from the Pírluna delta, using fleet power and Imperial privileges to keep the Free City free.

reasons: The clearest port-and-fleet theme among the four cities.
Delta trade gives the shared diplomatic route a distinct opening.
The campaign can continue into the B59 long route.
warnings: Only 2 missions are specific to A82; the other 20 are shared with the other small Luna countries.
Do not describe Pírluna as the main Luna River.

positive_indicators: Coastal defence and port public safety
values.rationale: Coastal defence, port safety, and Free City autonomy serve public interests, but the country's values focus more on local security and prosperity; alliance control and warfare make it less good than Bluehart and Bellacaire.
